findings.summary: The criterion-2 timing assertion runs against a stubbed global fetch and a mocked spawnWorker, so totalMs is milliseconds no matter what the implementation does; that assertion alone cannot go red. Discrimination for §1.1 is actually carried by two other places: the node_timeout<=30 guard read from workflow.yaml (red on the forbidden masking bump that sank attempt 2) and the PhaseTimings field assertions (red if instrumentation is reverted). Reverting the cause-elimination itself is caught by test/g6-result-timeout.test.ts:790-850, not here. Substantively covered, but a reader of this file alone would overestimate its discriminating power; a pointer comment to the g6 discriminant would make the coverage self-evident.

The phase budget in this comment block ('bus paging < 2s, CAS < 1s, spawn < 2s, total < 10s') reads as an estimate, while spec §1.1 lines 105-106 asks for measured numbers identifying where the 30 seconds went. The measured breakdown does exist at runtime — PhaseTimings is printed in --run stdout — so Z1 will produce it, but no committed artifact records the actual per-phase figures for the seed board.

readNodeTimeout is asserted as <= 30 as a hard ceiling. Spec line 111 does permit raising the engine-level bound if genuinely necessary, provided the change is made in workflow.yaml limits with a justified lower bound; this assertion would block that permitted path and force a test edit alongside it. Correct for this delivery, worth revisiting if a future package needs a larger engine bound.
